old: - The PGL(2) lemma and the resulting proof of HYP-9275's octahedron identity.
new: - The PGL(2) counting lemma and the resulting proof of HYP-9275's octahedron identity. The invariance behind it is classical: with an even in-degree orientation, `F(x) = χ(∏_{(i→j)} det(x_i, x_j))` in homogeneous coordinates, which is well defined on `P¹(F_q)` because every degree is even and `GL(2)`-invariant because `|E|` is even (the triangle case is the oriented Paley two-graph on `P¹(F_q)`; see e.g. Gunderson–Semeraro, arXiv:2204.10775, and Babai–Cameron on switching classes of tournaments).
why: Novelty overclaim: the Moebius invariance of even-degree chi-products is classical; the new part is the counting consequence and its use.

old: - **Part 7.** It is elementary. The class-count relations are standard for regular tournaments.
new: - **Part 7.** It is elementary and classical in substance: for regular `T`, `TT4 = n·C(k,3) − Σ_v c3(N⁺(v))` and `c4 = n(n²−1)(n−3)/48 − Σ_v c3(N⁺(v))`, so the bound is the known lower bound `c4(T) ≥ c4(DR_n)` on 4-cycles of regular tournaments, with the same equality case (see Savchenko, arXiv:2403.07629, §1, and the references there). The class-count relations are standard for regular tournaments.
why: The TT4 lemma is equivalent to a classical 4-cycle bound; cite it.
